statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of homepage, article, search, login and recovery templates.

page.notes: Public Italian Wikipedia. Server-rendered content with canonical MPA navigation and separate mobile-host affordance.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark media matches, but the page remains light with color-scheme normal.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, document.getAnimations() returned an empty list.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and visual inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast passes on both templates; controls and text remain visibly distinct.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS/runtime feature probe plus route screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: No view-transition rules were detected on conventional MPA navigation.
No scroll-linked effects or animation timelines were found, so the site does not implement scroll motion with blocking handlers.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM event and CSS behavior probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No pointer/touch inline handlers or gesture-heavy custom interaction was found; scrolling remains native.

checkOutcomes.method: Long-page screenshot, layout and CSS probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The very long article retains static chrome with no scroll-state/progress feature detected.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop visual inspection of menus and side panels
checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible menus and appearance controls remain aligned within the page chrome and do not drift or clip in the captured states.
Active tabs, article title, contents navigation, search result heading and focused skip link clearly orient the user.
No on-load modal, consent wall or interstitial obscures content.
No modal flow is imposed; disclosure/menu controls use native labelled inputs and buttons in the inspected states.
Article content dominates the central column; secondary tools are visibly separated and no decorative advertising competes with content.
Viewport is forced to 1120 CSS px and scaled to 0.3214 instead of reflowing.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS container-rule probe and narrow screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Probe found zero container rules; the same desktop columns are downscaled at 360px.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse target audit and focus probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Focus is visible, but Lighthouse reports two article target-size failures and narrow navigation is physically tiny.
Homepage identifies Wikipedia and offers search/browse paths; article, search and login pages have unambiguous titles and actions.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative search and authentication surface walkthrough
checkOutcomes.evidence: A populated search URL returns the expected Roma article/results surface; login exposes username, password, submit, account and recovery paths.
The nonexistent article clearly explains the state and offers search/create/refresh paths; login offers access help and password recovery.
Article Lighthouse LCP is 7.5s; homepage trace is fast, showing the failure is template/content-sensitive.
Homepage observed CLS 0.000215 and article Lighthouse CLS 0.
Homepage trace TBT is 5.49ms; both Lighthouse runs report 10ms TBT despite one article layout long task.
Blocking stylesheet and cache signals show avoidable delivery overhead.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse unused-code diagnostics and HAR weight
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 164 KiB unused JS and 75–79 KiB unused CSS; largest script is 325 KB transferred.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits and image DOM audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Missing alt, unnamed link, label and name-mismatch failures occur on representative pages.
Color contrast passes on homepage and article.

checkOutcomes.method: Heading/landmark probe, Lighthouse and programmatic focus
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heading order and one-main audits pass; focused skip link receives a 2px solid outline.
Text is downscaled with the entire 1120px canvas and is not comfortably legible.

checkOutcomes.method: Viewport DOM, Lighthouse target-size and mobile screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Fixed width=1120 prevents mobile reflow and article target-size audit fails.
Both representative Lighthouse runs report no browser console errors.
Doctype/charset pass, but many article images lack lazy loading/alt and one lacks dimensions.
Both runs report missing first-party source maps and an Inspector Issues failure; BFCache, paste and permission timing pass.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata probe and Lighthouse SEO
checkOutcomes.evidence: Titles pass, but meta descriptions are absent on homepage and article.
Links and robots are crawlable, but fixed width=1120 is not mobile friendly.

checkOutcomes.method: Canonical/hreflang probe and direct robots/sitemap fetch
checkOutcomes.evidence: Canonical and 200 status pass; hreflang is absent and /sitemap.xml returns 404.
The article exposes one JSON-LD block, five Open Graph tags and a canonical URL aligned to visible content.
HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff and no secrets pass; CSP allowances and one insecure session identifier weaken the posture.
No known tracker domains were found; third-party traffic is Wikimedia infrastructure rather than advertising analytics.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse permission audits and login DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No geolocation/notification prompts occur on load; username field advertises WebAuthn conditional UI via autocomplete="username webauthn".
Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent, and no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options defense is present.
Discoverability captures show 99–100% content coverage without JavaScript and no empty app shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative screenshots and Lighthouse runtime audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Core menus/content render without clipping on desktop; no console errors and BFCache audit passes.
Wikipedia is a public content MPA rather than an install-focused web app; no offline/installability requirement was inferred.
checkOutcomes.reason: Wikipedia is a public content MPA rather than an install-focused web app; no offline/installability requirement was inferred.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A nonexistent title produces a clear recovery page with search, create and refresh actions rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM language and multilingual UI inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The document declares lang=it and exposes extensive language navigation; reading order remains logical in inspected Italian templates.
Italian article numbers and dates are presented in Italian conventions and the site is explicitly language-localized.
The audited encyclopedia reading/search/login journeys contain no user-specific scheduling or time-zone-sensitive event flow.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited encyclopedia reading/search/login journeys contain no user-specific scheduling or time-zone-sensitive event flow.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual review across entry, article, search and login
checkOutcomes.evidence: No ads, confirmshaming, forced continuity, nagging consent or preselected commercial choice appears.
Login fields have explicit labels and password/access recovery links; nonexistent content explains the state without blame and offers next steps.
Login uses username webauthn and current-password autocomplete tokens and labels both credential fields.
No checkout, subscription, cancellation or sensitive authenticated account-management flow was in the unauthenticated representative scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No checkout, subscription, cancellation or sensitive authenticated account-management flow was in the unauthenticated representative scope.

checkOutcomes.method: Image audit and raw document size
checkOutcomes.evidence: Long article has 97 legacy-format images and 90 below-fold images without lazy loading.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse unused-code and HAR payload analysis
checkOutcomes.evidence: Reading pages ship substantial unused JS/CSS and a 325KB bundle.
No known trackers or autoplay media were found; third-party bytes are Wikimedia image infrastructure serving article content.
No developer intent for agent-executable actions was declared; for this emerging contextual principle, highly crawlable semantic content is sufficient and absence of WebMCP is not penalized.
checkOutcomes.reason: No developer intent for agent-executable actions was declared; for this emerging contextual principle, highly crawlable semantic content is sufficient and absence of WebMCP is not penalized.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The encyclopedia reading/search journeys do not require on-device generative inference; absence is an expected non-applicable opportunity.
checkOutcomes.reason: The encyclopedia reading/search journeys do not require on-device generative inference; absence is an expected non-applicable opportunity.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited canonical experience is an MPA with full-document navigation and no representative long-lived repeatable SPA/modal interaction; a synthetic loop would not establish real leak risk.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited canonical experience is an MPA with full-document navigation and no representative long-lived repeatable SPA/modal interaction; a synthetic loop would not establish real leak risk.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The large 2.09MB article uses about 40.3MB heap snapshot self size for 18,989 DOM elements; footprint is substantial but proportionate to a uniquely long media-rich article.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap constructor and runtime handler inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap summary top constructors contains no Detached* population and runtime probe found zero inline handlers; no accumulation signal exists in the inspected stable state.

principleOutcomes.reason: No developer intent for agent-executable actions was declared; for this emerging contextual principle, highly crawlable semantic content is sufficient and absence of WebMCP is not penalized. The encyclopedia reading/search journeys do not require on-device generative inference; absence is an expected non-applicable opportunity.

paths.description: Canonical homepage: primary navigation, search entry, content overview and global chrome.
Long encyclopedic article template: highest-risk content, media, performance, indexing and reading journey.
Search/result journey represented by a query for Roma.

findings.summary: The default experience ignores the operating-system dark preference.
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the probe reports body background rgb(248,249,250), color-scheme normal, while the screenshot remains light and the appearance panel selects “Chiaro”.
findings.suggestedFix: Default the theme control to “Automatico”, declare color-scheme: light dark, and apply system-driven color tokens; retain explicit user overrides.

findings.summary: Page and state changes have no transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The preferences/source probe found no view-transition rules and desktop navigation is a conventional abrupt MPA swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin article/search navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long article chrome does not communicate reading progress or react to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The 101,424 CSS-pixel article is shown with a static header/sidebar; the CSS probe found no container or scroll-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading-progress affordance or scroll-state-aware sticky article chrome, preserving reduced-motion behavior.

findings.summary: The desktop host forces a 1120 CSS-pixel canvas on a 360px mobile viewport, shrinking the entire page to 32%.
findings.evidence: Both home and article layout captures report innerWidth/clientWidth 1120 and visualViewport scale 0.3214 at a requested 360x800 viewport; screenshots show unreadably tiny multi-column pages. The live viewport meta is width=1120.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve width=device-width on this host and reflow Vector/article layouts to one column at narrow widths instead of relying on whole-page downscaling or a separate mobile-host link.

findings.summary: Some article touch targets are too small or too tightly spaced.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse article accessibility reports two target-size failures; the 360px screenshot shows dense, tiny navigation links caused by the fixed 1120px viewport. Keyboard focus itself is visible with a 2px outline.
findings.suggestedFix: After fixing viewport reflow, ensure interactive targets meet accessible size/spacing guidance and preserve :focus-visible outlines.

findings.summary: The representative long article misses the good LCP range on Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured article LCP 7.5s, FCP 4.8s and performance score 0.62, despite low TBT and zero CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the article LCP request chain, prioritise the LCP asset/content, and reduce render-blocking and unused payload before it.

findings.summary: The load includes avoidable blocking and cache-delivery overhead.
findings.evidence: The HAR identifies three parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, reports multiple image responses without useful cache headers, and transfers 748,407 bytes across 65 requests on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical CSS chains, confirm/retain deferred script loading, and give immutable thumbnail responses effective cache headers where infrastructure permits.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JavaScript and CSS are shipped to reading pages.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 164 KiB unused JavaScript and 75–79 KiB unused CSS; the HAR’s largest script transfers 325,000 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Split ResourceLoader bundles by actual page capability and defer editing, popup, analytics, and visual-editor modules until interaction requires them.

findings.summary: Representative pages contain unnamed links/images and an unlabelled search field.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 20 missing image alts and six unnamed links on the homepage; the article reports three missing alts, two unnamed links, one label failure and one accessible-name mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images and controls names, use empty alt only for truly decorative images, and associate the search input with a persistent label.

findings.summary: Text is not legible at the audited narrow form factor.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the fixed 1120px layout is scaled to 0.3214; article and search body copy renders only a few physical pixels high in screenshots.
findings.suggestedFix: Use device-width reflow, a readable minimum text size and comfortable line lengths; collapse sidebars rather than scaling them with article content.

findings.summary: The fixed-width viewport prevents effective mobile reflow and compounds target-size failures.
findings.evidence: The article declares viewport width=1120 rather than device-width; Lighthouse reports target-size failures and mobile screenshots show whole-page scaling rather than reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed viewport with width=device-width,initial-scale=1 and verify 320px reflow and 200% zoom without loss of content or function.

findings.summary: Article image delivery has avoidable semantics and loading inefficiencies.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found one missing dimension, 90 below-fold images without lazy loading, five images without srcset and 69 images without alt among 100 article images.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, retain responsive source sets, and distinguish decorative empty alt from missing alternatives.

findings.summary: First-party production bundles lack usable source maps and trigger DevTools inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Both Lighthouse runs report four missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript files and one Inspector Issues failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish protected production source maps or provide correct sourceMappingURL endpoints, then resolve the reported browser issue.

findings.summary: Public landing and article pages omit meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The article DOM probe returns description:null; both Lighthouse SEO runs fail meta-description while titles are descriptive.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, page-specific meta descriptions from stable lead content for the homepage and article template.

findings.summary: Pages are crawlable but the desktop host is not mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse confirms indexing and crawlable anchors, but the viewport is width=1120 and the 360px evidence shows a scaled desktop canvas.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a device-width viewport and responsive template on canonical desktop URLs so mobile users and mobile indexing receive a usable page.

findings.summary: Localized article pages omit hreflang and the host exposes no sitemap at /sitemap.xml.
findings.evidence: The Italia article has a canonical URL but zero hreflang link elements; /sitemap.xml returns HTTP 404 while robots.txt is valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose reciprocal hreflang signals for language variants and document or publish the appropriate sitemap/index discovery mechanism for this large public corpus.

findings.summary: Transport is strong, but client policy and cookie posture have avoidable weaknesses.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; the cookie capture includes itwikimwuser-sessionId without Secure/HttpOnly and all seven observed cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe CSP allowances through nonces/hashes and eliminate or harden the insecure session identifier; scope SameSite=None only to cookies that require cross-site use.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defense headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The header capture reports no Referrer-Policy, no Permissions-Policy and no X-Frame-Options; the CSP shown also has no frame-ancestors directive.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and add CSP frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options fallback) according to Wikimedia embedding requirements.

findings.summary: The long article loads many below-fold legacy-format images eagerly.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 97 of 100 images in legacy formats and 90 below-fold images without loading=lazy; the DOM itself is about 2.09 MB raw HTML.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold figures and negotiate modern encoded thumbnails where quality and browser support allow, while preserving SVG sources for maps and diagrams.

findings.summary: Reading pages download capability bundles that Lighthouse identifies as mostly unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 164 KiB unused JavaScript and up to 79 KiB unused CSS; the homepage HAR’s largest JS bundle transfers 325 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-reading features behind interaction and deprioritise optional background, analytics, preview and editing modules.

taskList.title: Replace the fixed 1120px viewport with genuine narrow-screen reflow
Fix accessible names, labels and image alternatives
Reduce article LCP and split unused reading-page bundles
Harden CSP, cookies and browser defense headers
Lazy-load and modernize below-fold article image delivery
Honor system dark mode by default
Add descriptions and complete localized indexing signals
Publish usable production source maps and clear Inspector issues
